newsitem.title: USA: PSA calls new yield burning report "misguided".
newsitem.headline: PSA calls new yield burning report "misguided".

text.p: A municipal bond industry looby group on Tuesday said that Los Angeles County's latest report on yield burning in the municipal bond market is "misguided."

"It's a very lengthy document and we're still going through it. But it looks like once again they are focusing on broad brush issues and avoiding the need to look at (the situation) on a case-by-case basis," Micah Green, executive vice president of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, said.
Green was referring to a report issued on Tuesday by lawyers for the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority.

The lawyers had charged in December that bond dealers made nearly $1 billion in improper profits from yield burning since 1990 from issuees around the country, and they reported on Tuesday that they had corroborated those findings after reviewing the data.
But Green rejected the findings by the lawyers, Phillips & Cohen.

"Phillips & Cohen's approach continues to be that they (the deals) are all bad," Green said. "They are not all bad. This is a is a great marketplace. If there are bad transactions out there, the regulators should go after them."
Green noted that bond firms refuse to supply Phillips & Cohen with additional data on individual deals. But the law firm also has refused dealers' requests for background data on its study, he said.

"Our members are under investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission and Internal Revenue Service," Green said. "It would be ludicrous for anyone involved in an investigation to publicly air data that's relevant to that investigation," Green said. "They, as good lawyers, know that," Green said.
"We need to see their data because they are using their data to publicly trash this marketplace," Green said.
